chapter.li: LEChapter1 Verse1 Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, according to the promise of life which is in Christ Jesus, VerseEnd Verse2 to Timothy, my dearly beloved son: Grace, mercy, and peace, from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord. VerseEnd

Verse3 I thank God, whom I serve from my forefathers with pure conscience, that without ceasing I have remembrance of you in my prayers night and day, VerseEnd Verse4 greatly desiring to see you, being mindful of your tears, that I may be filled with joy VerseEnd Verse5 when I call to remembrance the unfeigned faith that is in you, which dwelled first in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice, and I am persuaded that in you also. VerseEnd Verse6 Wherefore, I put you in remembrance that you stir up the gift of God which is in you by the putting on of my hands. VerseEnd Verse7 For God has not given us the spirit of fear, but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind. VerseEnd

Verse8 Be not therefore ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me his prisoner, but be partaker of the afflictions of the gospel according to the power of God, VerseEnd Verse9 who has saved us and called us with a holy calling — not according to our works, but according to his own purpose and grace — which was given us in Christ Jesus before the world began, VerseEnd Verse10 but is now made manifest by the appearing of our Savior Jesus Christ, who has abolished death and has brought life and immortality to light through the gospel, VerseEnd Verse11 of which I am appointed a preacher, and an apostle, and a teacher of the Gentiles, VerseEnd Verse12 for which cause I also suffer these things. Nevertheless, I am not ashamed, for I know whom I have believed, and am persuaded that he is able to keep that which I have committed unto him against that day. VerseEnd

Verse13 Hold fast the form of sound words which you have heard of me in faith and love which is in Christ Jesus. VerseEnd Verse14 That good thing which was committed unto you, keep by the holy ghost which dwells in us. VerseEnd Verse15 This you know: that all they who are in Asia are turned away from me, of whom are Phygelus and Hermogenes. VerseEnd Verse16 The Lord give mercy unto the house of Onesiphorus, for he oft refreshed me and was not ashamed of my chain, VerseEnd Verse17 but when he was in Rome, he sought me out very diligently and found me. VerseEnd Verse18 The Lord grant unto him that he may find mercy of the Lord in that day. And in how many things he ministered unto me at Ephesus, you know very well. VerseEnd

LEChapter2 Verse1 Therefore, my son, be strong in the grace that is in Christ Jesus. VerseEnd Verse2 And the things that you have heard of me among many witnesses, the same commit you to faithful men who shall be able to teach others also. VerseEnd Verse3 Therefore, endure hardship as a good soldier of Jesus Christ. VerseEnd Verse4 No man that wars entangles himself with the affairs of this life, that he may please him who has chosen him to be a soldier. VerseEnd Verse5 And if a man also strive for masteries, he is not crowned except he strive lawfully. VerseEnd Verse6 The husbandman that labors must be partaker of the fruits. VerseEnd Verse7 Consider what I say, and the Lord give you understanding in all things. VerseEnd Verse8 Remember that Jesus Christ, of the seed of David, was raised from the dead according to the gospel, VerseEnd Verse9 wherein I suffer trouble as an evil doer, even unto bonds — but the word of God is not bound. VerseEnd Verse10 Therefore, I endure all things for the elect’s sakes, that they may also obtain the salvation which is in Christ Jesus with eternal glory, VerseEnd Verse11 for this is a faithful saying: If we are dead with him, we shall also live with him. VerseEnd Verse12 If we suffer, we shall also reign with him. If we deny him, he also will deny us. VerseEnd Verse13 If we believe not, yet he abides faithful. He cannot deny himself. VerseEnd

Verse14 Of these things put them in remembrance, charging them before the Lord that they quarrel not about words to no profit, but to the subverting of the hearers. VerseEnd Verse15 Strive to show yourself approved unto God, a workman that need not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth. VerseEnd Verse16 But shun worldly and vain babblings, for they will increase unto more ungodliness. VerseEnd Verse17 And their word will eat as does a canker, of whom is Hymenaeus and Philetus, VerseEnd Verse18 who concerning the truth have erred — saying that the resurrection is past already — and overthrow the faith of some. VerseEnd Verse19 Nevertheless, the foundation of God stands sure, having this seal: The Lord knows them that are his. And let everyone that names the name of Christ depart from iniquity. VerseEnd

Verse20 But in a great house, there are not only vessels of gold and of silver, but also of wood and of earth, and some to honor and some to dishonor. VerseEnd Verse21 If a man therefore purge himself from these, he shall be a vessel unto honor, sanctified and meet for the master’s use, and prepared unto every good work. VerseEnd Verse22 Flee also youthful lusts, but follow righteousness, faith, charity, peace, with them that call on the Lord out of a pure heart. VerseEnd Verse23 But foolish and unlearned discussions avoid, knowing that they do engender strifes. VerseEnd Verse24 And the servant of the Lord must not quarrel, but be gentle unto all men, apt to teach, patient, VerseEnd Verse25 in meekness instructing those that oppose them, if God perhaps will give them repentance to the acknowledging of the truth VerseEnd Verse26 and that they may recover themselves out of the snare of the devil, who are taken captive by him at his will. VerseEnd

LEChapter3 Verse1 This know also: that in the last days, perilous times shall come; VerseEnd Verse2 for men shall be lovers of their own selves, covetous, boasters, proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful, unholy, VerseEnd Verse3 without natural affection, trucebreakers, false accusers, without self-control, fierce, despisers of those that are good, VerseEnd Verse4 traitors, headstrong, haughty, lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God, VerseEnd Verse5 having a form of godliness but denying the power thereof. From such turn away, VerseEnd Verse6 for of this sort are they who creep into houses and lead captive silly women loaded with sins, led away with diverse lusts, VerseEnd Verse7 ever learning and never able to come to the knowledge of the truth. VerseEnd Verse8 Now as Jannes and Jambres withstood Moses, so do these also resist the truth: men of corrupt minds, reprobate concerning the faith. VerseEnd Verse9 But they shall proceed no further, for their folly shall be manifest unto all men, as theirs also was. VerseEnd

Verse10 But you have fully known my doctrine, manner of life, purpose, faith, long-suffering, charity, patience, VerseEnd Verse11 persecutions, afflictions which came unto me at Antioch, at Iconium, at Lystra — what persecutions I endured. But out of them all, the Lord delivered me. VerseEnd Verse12 Yea, and all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution; VerseEnd Verse13 for evil men and seducers shall wax worse and worse, deceiving and being deceived. VerseEnd Verse14 But continue in the things which you have learned and have been assured of, knowing of whom you have learned VerseEnd Verse15 them and that from a child you have known the holy scriptures, which are able to make you wise unto salvation through faith which is in Christ Jesus. VerseEnd Verse16 And all scripture given by inspiration of God is profitable — for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness, VerseEnd Verse17 that the man of God may be perfect, thoroughly furnished unto all good works. VerseEnd

LEChapter4 Verse1 I charge you therefore before God and the Lord Jesus Christ, who shall judge the quick and the dead at his appearing in his kingdom: VerseEnd Verse2 Preach the word, be ready in season. Those who are out of season, reprove, rebuke, exhort with all long-suffering and doctrine, VerseEnd Verse3 for the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine, but after their own lusts shall they heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears. VerseEnd Verse4 And they shall turn away their ears from the truth and shall be turned unto fables. VerseEnd Verse5 But watch yourself in all things, endure afflictions, do the work of an evangelist, make full proof of your ministry; VerseEnd Verse6 for I am now about to be offered and the time of my departure is at hand. VerseEnd Verse7 I have fought a good fight. I have finished my course. I have kept the faith. VerseEnd Verse8 Henceforth there is laid up for me a crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, shall give me at that day — and not to me only, but unto all them also that love his appearing. VerseEnd

Verse9 Do your diligence to come shortly unto me, VerseEnd Verse10 for Demas has forsaken me — having loved this present world — and is departed unto Thessalonica, Crescens to Galatia, Titus unto Dalmatia. VerseEnd Verse11 Only Luke is with me. Take Mark and bring him with you, for he is profitable to me for the ministry. VerseEnd Verse12 And Tychicus have I sent to Ephesus. VerseEnd Verse13 The cloak that I left at Troas with Carpus, when you come, bring with you, and the books, but especially the parchments. VerseEnd Verse14 Alexander the coppersmith did me much evil; the Lord reward him according to his works, VerseEnd Verse15 of whom be wary also, for he has greatly withstood our words. VerseEnd Verse16 At my first answer, no man stood with me, but all forsook me. I pray God that it may not be laid to their charge. VerseEnd Verse17 Notwithstanding, the Lord stood with me and strengthened me, that by me the preaching might be fully known and that all the Gentiles might hear. And I was delivered out of the mouth of the lion, VerseEnd Verse18 and the Lord shall deliver me from every evil work and will preserve me unto his Heavenly kingdom, to whom be glory for ever and ever. Amen. VerseEnd

Verse19 Salute Prisca, and Aquila, and the household of Onesiphorus. VerseEnd Verse20 Erastus abided at Corinth, but Trophimus have I left at Miletus sick. VerseEnd Verse21 Do your diligence to come before winter. Eubulus greets you, and Pudens, and Linus, and Claudia, and all the brethren. VerseEnd Verse22 The Lord Jesus Christ be with you and grace be with you all. Amen. VerseEnd

p.i: The second epistle unto Timothy, ordained the first bishop of the church of the Ephesians, was written from Rome when Paul was brought before Nero the second time.
